key_insight: Visual generators do not just need better rendering—they need a way to search beyond their training data when faced with open-ended, long-tailed user requests. This paper argues that agentic visual generation should evolve its knowledge boundary by integrating search to fill in missing world knowledge.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the structural limitation of visual generation models that confidently hallucinate unfamiliar entities, events, and concepts because they are trained on fixed corpora. It targets failures across new characters, trending topics, post-cutoff events, and other long-tail visual requests.
method: Builds SearchGen-20K and SearchGen-Bench: 20,839 prompts covering 12 failure categories and 22 domains.
Pairs prompts with pre-executed search evidence to study and evaluate search-augmented visual generation.
Frames visual generation as an agentic process that can actively retrieve external knowledge instead of relying only on internal training data.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work provides a concrete benchmark and task setup for reducing hallucinations in visual generation. It is useful for building more reliable multimodal agents that can handle real-world, constantly changing user requests.

paper_title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
paper_authors: Haozhe Wang, Weijia Feng, Jinpeng Yu, Che Liu, Ping Nie
